summary_en: Response to a dubium (Dubia section, no protocol or date printed) ruling that where particular calendars assign the celebration of the B.V.M. Queen of Apostles to the Saturday after the Ascension, it is kept on the Saturday after the Sixth Sunday of Easter where the Ascension is on Thursday, and on the Saturday after the Seventh Sunday of Easter where the Ascension is transferred to that Sunday. Recorded as kind other because it is an interpretative response affecting the date of a celebration in particular calendars, not a decree; the page prints no page number (52 taken from the table of contents).
excerpt: R. In locis in quibus habetur celebratio B.M.V. Reginae Apostolorum, eadem celebratio sabbato quod sequitur Ascensionem Domini, peragi debet, scilicet: a) Sabbato post dominicam VI Paschae, in locis in quibus Ascensio Domini feria V eiusdem hebdomadae celebratur; b) Sabbato post dominicam VII Paschae, in locis in quibus Ascensio Domini dominicae VII Paschae assignatur.

summary_en: The Sacred Congregation for the Clergy confirmed the decisions of the Mexican Episcopal Conference on weekday holy days of obligation: Epiphany is assigned to the Sunday between 2 and 8 January, the Ascension to the Seventh Sunday of Easter and Corpus Christi to the Sunday after Trinity; St Joseph, Sts Peter and Paul, the Assumption, All Saints and the Immaculate Conception cease to be of obligation; Mary Mother of God (1 January), Our Lady of Guadalupe (12 December) and Christmas remain of obligation. Printed as the headnote to a pastoral reflection by Bishop Arturo Szymanski of Tampico.
excerpt: Die 18 ianuarii 1978, Prot. 157210/I, Sacra Congregatio pro Clericis confirmavit ea, quae a Conferentia Episcoporum Mexici statuta fuerant de celebrationibus, quae infra hebdomadam sunt de praecepto servandae. Qua de re in dioecesibus Mexici: 1. Dominicae, tamquam diei proprio, assignantur Sollemnitates quae sequuntur, hac ratione: a) Epiphania, dominicae a die 2 ad diem 8 ianuarii occurrenti; b) Ascensio, dominicae VII Paschae; c) sollemnitas Ss.mi Corporis et Sanguinis Christi, dominicae post Ss.mam Trinitatem.

celebration.name_latin: Ss. Ioannes Fisher, episcopus, et Thomas Morus, martyres; S. Paulinus, episcopus

summary_en: Corrigendum (Varia, no protocol or date of its own) on the O.S.B. proper calendar for 22 June: the calendar printed in the Thesaurus Liturgiae Horarum monasticae (1977, confirmed 10 February 1977, Prot. CD 1415/76) shows only the optional memorial of Sts John Fisher and Thomas More, while the calendar in the Proprium Missarum ad usum Confoederationis O.S.B. (1975) shows the optional memorial of St Paulinus; the Congregation rules that the calendar printed in the Proprium Missarum, confirmed 22 June 1972 (Prot. n. 829/72), must be followed, the mention of St Paulinus of Nola having been dropped from the Thesaurus by a typographical accident. The opening page prints no page number (499 taken from the table of contents). Marked for review: a clarification rather than a decree.
excerpt: B. Calendarium proprium O.S.B. — Die 22 iunii, Calendarium O.S.B., quod invenitur in Thesauro Liturgiae Horarum monasticae, Romae 1977, p. 31 [...] veluti memoriam ad libitum illam indicat Ss. Ioannis Fisher, episcopi, et Thomae More, martyrum. E contra, Calendarium quod invenitur in capite Proprii Missarum ad usum Confoederationis O.S.B., Romae, 1975, p. 7, eodem die 22 iunii memoriam alteram ad libitum indicat: S. Paulini, episcopi. Quodnam Calendarium sequendum? R. Evidens est quod servari debent indicationes Calendarii publici iuris facti in capite Proprii Missarum, pp. 5-11, iuxta confirmationem a Sacra Congregatione pro Cultu Divino datam (Prot. n. 829/72 diei 22 iunii 1972).
